title: The role of organisational culture in facilitating agile and digital transformation: An empirical study based on survey and interview data
summary: Background: Digital transformation is essential for competitiveness in a rapidly changing business landscape, while organisational culture can enable or constrain its success. Objectives: The research investigated the influence of organisational culture, as an independent variable, on organisational performance in digital transformation initiatives within medium-to-large software development organisations. Method: A convergent mixed-methods design combined a survey (N = 315) with 18 semi-structured interviews involving professionals in agile and digital initiatives. SPSS was used for reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), bivariate correlations, and multivariate regression to examine relationships between variables. Interview transcripts were thematically coded and analysed in ATLAS.ti. Results: The empirical results indicated that culture practices were positively associated with a supportive agile (Pearson r ≈ 0.32). Simple regression showed culture significantly predicted agile (R2 ≈ 0.10). A multiple regression predicting digital transformation outcomes from culture and agile was significant (R2 ≈ 0.40), with agile the stronger unique predictor and culture adding a smaller but meaningful contribution. The qualitative analysis showed that organisational culture is a fundamental but indirect factor in digital transformation. Conclusion: The study measured how culture influences agile methodology’s role in digital transformation, highlighting its impact on success in various corporate environments. Contribution: The findings position organisational culture as a key enabling condition, rather than a direct cause, of digital transformation outcomes. Managers should therefore embed cultural goals in agile roadmaps, standardise essential routines, and minimise structural hand-offs to sustain improvements across teams.

title: Digital Transformation in Islamic Education Management: A Review of Governance Innovation and Quality Improvement in Islamic Educational Institutions
summary: Digital transformation has become increasingly important in Islamic education management; however, existing research remains fragmented across digital leadership, information systems, administrative accountability, and educational quality assurance. This study aims to develop an integrated understanding of how digital transformation contributes to governance innovation and quality improvement in Islamic educational institutions. It employed a qualitative integrative literature review, drawing on scholarly publications from 2021 to 2026. Candidate sources were identified through academic search platforms, journal websites, DOI records, and publisher pages. Relevant literature was screened according to its scholarly credibility, verifiability, and substantive relevance to digital governance, institutional management, and educational quality. Data were organized in an analytical matrix and examined through qualitative thematic synthesis to identify recurring patterns, relationships, and conceptual implications. The findings reveal five interrelated dimensions of digital transformation: digital leadership and organizational readiness; integrated information systems and data-driven decision-making; administrative efficiency, transparency, and accountability; Islamic values and digital ethics; and quality assurance and continuous improvement. The synthesis further identifies three interconnected management components—digital leadership, data-driven governance, and digital quality assurance—supported by institutional capacity and Islamic ethical principles. These components form a continuous improvement cycle in which leadership establishes strategic priorities, reliable data informs institutional decisions, and quality assurance guides evaluation and corrective action. The study concludes that digital transformation should be understood as an institution-wide governance process rather than merely the adoption of technological platforms. Its conceptual framework offers a basis for context-sensitive management strategies, although empirical validation is required to establish its applicability across diverse Islamic educational institutions.

title: Reimagining Sustainable Natural Resource Governance through the Paradigm of Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘ah and Ecological Justice
summary: The exploitation of natural resources and environmental degradation call for sustainable governance grounded in ethical and normative values. This study aims to identify Islamic principles in responding to contemporary environmental governance challenges and their relevance to sustainable natural resource management. This study employs a qualitative-descriptive approach through an integrative literature review of 25 scientific publications, primarily from 2021–2026, using content analysis and thematic synthesis. The results indicate that there are eight sustainable governance strategies closely linked to Islamic values within the framework of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, including public interest-based planning, regulation, participation, accountability, and law enforcement which reflect the principles of justice (‘adl) and stewardship (amānah),pollution monitoring, ecosystem restoration, and sustainability evaluation grounded in the principles of balance (mīzān) and ecological stewardship (khilāfah). summary: The study investigated the effect of sustainability reporting on the corporate performance of companies quoted on the Nigerian Stock Exchange. The measures for corporate performance used in the study are profit margin (PM) and market value indicated by share price (SP). The three dimensions of sustainability reporting examined are namely; economic, social, and environmental disclosures. The ex-post factor research design was employed and after filtering the population of listed companies, a sample of 70 listed companies drawn from oil and gas, telecommunication, and manufacturing industries in Nigeria with complete and comprehensive data for the period under review (2010-2019) was used for the study. A series of preliminary analyses such as descriptive statistics, correlation, and multicollinearity analysis were first conducted. Next, the panel co-integration test was conducted to examine the presence of a longrun relationship between the variables, and then finally the panel regression was conducted to examine the relationship between sustainability reporting and corporate performance. The findings of the study revealed that (i) Economic performance disclosure and social performance disclosure have a significant positive effect on the net profit margin of companies listed on the Nigeria Stock Exchange (ii) Environmental performance disclosure has no significant effect on the net profit margin of companies listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange, (iii) Economic performance disclosure and social performance disclosure has a significant positive effect on the market value of companies listed on the Nigeria Stock Exchange, (iv) Environmental performance disclosure has no significant effect on market value of companies listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange The study recommends that environmental disclosures have been lagging critically behind economic and social disclosure, thus companies need to pay more attention to addressing and disclosing on their environment. The study also recommends that there should be some regulation on environmental disclosures by the government for companies in Nigeria and companies should endeavour to improve not just economic disclosures but the quality of these disclosures.

title: Shared Beliefs, Harmonious Outcomes: The Role of Corporate National Spirit Narrative in Shaping Online Consumer Complaints
summary: ABSTRACT In the digital and multicultural era, online consumer complaints play a pivotal role in corporate sustainability. This study analyzes over 16 million consumer complaints from 2018 to 2023, constructing indicators for corporate national spirit narrative and consumer complaints in China's A‐share listed companies using machine learning and text analysis. Applying social exchange theory, we find that corporate national spirit narrative significantly reduces online consumer complaints. The key mechanism is that, by publicly expressing national spirit, firms signal their commitment to shared national values and social responsibility, thereby enhancing employee satisfaction and corporate market reputation. Heterogeneity analysis shows a stronger effect in firms with more employee stock ownership, businesses with greater consumer importance, and downstream firms in the supply chain. Additionally, the effects vary across complaint types and dimensions of national spirit. This study provides novel theoretical insights and empirical evidence for managing consumer complaints and advancing corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices in the digital age.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF REFLEXIVE ENTERPRISE MANAGEMENT IN THE CONTEXT OF ENSURING ECONOMIC SECURITY: FUNCTIONAL FOUNDATIONS AND THE SECTORAL CONTEXT OF FOREIGN INVESTMENT
summary: Digital transformation changes the informational and analytical conditions under which enterprises observe their own activities, interpret deviations and revise managerial decisions. This issue is especially relevant for economies competing for foreign investment while simultaneously facing heightened cyber, data and investment-security risks. The purpose of the article is to develop a conceptual and analytical framework for examining how digital technologies alter the information, analytical, reflexive, decision and control functions of reflexive enterprise management, and to clarify the relevance of those functions to the preparation, implementation and monitoring of foreign investment. The study distinguishes digital data capture and automated analytics from managerial reflexivity: technology can extend the evidence base, increase traceability and accelerate monitoring, but it does not itself perform critical reassessment of assumptions. The methodological design combines an integrative review of reflexive management learning, double-loop learning, team reflexivity and digital-transformation research with functional decomposition of the management process. The foreign-investment dimension is examined across the stages of investor interest, due diligence, project preparation and structuring, investment decision, implementation, monitoring, adjustment and possible reinvestment or exit. Economic security is considered at two analytically separate levels: digital-operational security of the enterprise and investment-security constraints related to foreign control, critical assets and sensitive technologies. Official Ukrainian enterprise ICT statistics and National Bank of Ukraine foreign-direct-investment statistics are used solely for sectoral contextualisation of the digital and investment environment. The empirical material is descriptive and is not treated as a direct measure of organisational reflexivity or as evidence of a causal effect of management practices on FDI. The article is therefore designed as a conceptual-analytical study with empirical sectoral contextualisation and establishes a transparent basis for subsequent firm-level testing of reflexive management practices and investment outcomes.

title: Sustainable Supply Chain Economics and Global Market Adaptation Strategies
summary: The application of sustainable supply chain management is increasingly becoming a common approach for increasing efficiency, effectiveness, and resilience in an environment that is highly uncertain in terms of the global markets. In this research, the use of sustainable supply chain management approaches for the purpose of adaptation to the global market by means of green sourcing, resource efficiency, diversification of suppliers, regionalization, digital visibility, and flexibility is studied. An integrative conceptual framework is developed, linking the performance in sustainability to economic efficiency and supply chain resilience. The research further highlights the significance of regional adaptation and the adoption of circular practices as ways of minimizing costs and increasing competitiveness in the long run. The model proposed in this paper brings together all the elements needed to understand the interaction between sustainability and adaptation to global markets. The results indicate that organizations that combine environmental considerations with economic and adaptive competencies can increase supply reliability, decrease risk exposure, be more efficient with resources, and experience sustainable growth in their competitiveness.

title: Decoupled ore and scrap trade networks constrain low-carbon metal supply
summary: Abstract Global supply chains for critical metals such as aluminium and copper are increasingly exposed to sustainability and geopolitical risks under the pressure of energy transition. In this paper we compare primary (ore) and secondary (scrap) trade networks for the United States, European Union and China using multilayer network analysis. We focus on the years 2010-2023, a period that captures intensified demand for the two metals. Results identify a marked structural decoupling: around 40% of scrap-trading countries do not participate in ore trade. Further, while about 50% of ore trade links overlap with scrap networks, only some 10–15% of scrap connections overlap with ore trade. Despite strong alignment in trading partners, volumes of scrap and ore trade diverge substantially. The observed differences indicate that the two commodity streams use partly distinct international trading relationships. Major economies may compete for ore suppliers but remain interdependent in scrap trade, revealing a bifurcated system with uneven resilience. Strengthening integration between primary and secondary supply chains is therefore critical for achieving sustainable critical metal supply for the low-carbon energy transition and establishing resource-efficient metal systems.

title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
summary: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience, and customer emotional intelligence) lead to strengthening the fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities. Also, the pivotal phenomenon (fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities), individual-marketing factors, and technological factors lead to strengthening customer acumen (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors). Finally, it was determined that customer intelligence (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors) leads to a reduction in undesirable behavioral-reactive outcomes and a strengthening of desirable behavioral-reactive outcomes.Originality/Value: According to the results obtained from the implementation of the qualitative and quantitative parts of the research, the variables 1) deceptive advertising, 2) customer emotional intelligence, 3) customer respect for the brand, 4) buyer confusion, 5) brand uniqueness, 6) brand community, 7) brand love, 8) brand attachment, 9) customer thirst for shopping, 10) market rumor management, 11) digital age, 12) negative internal emotions, 13) customer mental anxiety, 14) interaction-communication problems, and 15) customer resentment, 16) brand responsibility are considered new research findings.

summary: على الرغم من تنامي الاهتمام البحثي بالتحول الرقمي، تظل الدراسات الكمية التي تفحص أثر أبعاده المتكاملة على كفاءة إدارة الموارد البشرية في البيئة السعودية محدودة. تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى قياس أثر أبعاد التحول الرقمي على كفاءة إدارة الموارد البشرية في منظمات القطاعين الحكومي وشبه الحكومي والخاص بمدينة جدة، في ظل محدودية الدراسات الميدانية التي تناولت هذه العلاقة في البيئة السعودية بصورة شاملة. واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، وطُورت استبانة وفق مقياس ليكرت الخماسي، وطُبقت إلكترونياً على عينة قصدية بلغت (40) مفردة من العاملين في القطاعات المستهدفة. وأظهرت نتائج اختبار الثبات أن معاملات كرونباخ ألفا تراوحت بين (0.877–0.915) لأبعاد الدراسة، وبلغت (0.965) للأداة ككل، كما تأكد صدق البناء باستخدام معاملات ارتباط بيرسون، مما يعكس ارتفاع مستوى الاتساق الداخلي للأداة. وأظهرت النتائج ارتفاع مستوى توافر أبعاد التحول الرقمي بصورة عامة، حيث جاءت البنية التحتية التقنية في المرتبة الأولى، بينما جاءت المهارات والقدرات الرقمية في المرتبة الأخيرة بدرجة متوسطة. كما سجل بُعد الرضا الوظيفي والتعلم المستمر أعلى متوسطات أبعاد إدارة الموارد البشرية، تلاه بُعد كفاءة إدارة الموارد البشرية. وأكدت نتائج تحليل الانحدار المتعدد وجود أثر ذي دلالة إحصائية لجميع أبعاد التحول الرقمي على إدارة الموارد البشرية، حيث مثّلت القيادة التحويلية والثقافة التنظيمية أقوى المتغيرات تفسيراً للتباين، تلتها المهارات والقدرات الرقمية، ثم البنية التحتية التقنية، وأخيراً الاستراتيجية والحوكمة الرقمية، مع تفسير النماذج نسبة مقدارها R²=0.456 من التباين في المتغير التابع، وبلغت قيمة F(4,35)=7.341 عند مستوى دلالة إحصائية (p<0.001).

title: DETERMINAN PENGELOLAAN KEUANGAN GENERASI Z DI DESA TUNGGARA, BANJARNEGARA
summary: Sound financial management is an essential competence for Generation Z, who grow up in a digital environment with heavy exposure to consumption trends. This study examines the effects of financial literacy, hedonistic lifestyle, self-control, Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), and financial technology (fintech) on the financial management of Generation Z in Tunggara Village, Banjarnegara Regency. A quantitative survey design was used. Primary data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire distributed via Google Forms to 100 respondents aged 16–29 years, selected by purposive sampling from a population of 479, and analyzed with multiple linear regression. Financial literacy (B = 0.591; p < 0.001), self-control (B = 0.165; p < 0.001), and fintech (B = 0.142; p = 0.010) have positive and significant effects on financial management, whereas hedonistic lifestyle (p = 0.614) and FoMO (p = 0.675) have no significant effect. The model is feasible (F = 57.954; p < 0.001) and explains 75.5% of the variance in financial management. Financial literacy is the most dominant determinant (standardized beta = 0.561). The findings highlight the need for applied financial education, stronger self-control, and prudent fintech use among rural Generation Z.

title: External Environmental Audits and Supply‐Chain Carbon Monitoring: Cross‐Country Evidence on Corporate Environmental Accountability
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines external energy audits and reported supply‐chain carbon monitoring using 12,154 energy‐monitoring establishments in 37 countries from the 2019‐coded World Bank Enterprise Survey cross‐section. Audit is associated with an 8.1‐percentage‐point higher monitoring probability after establishment, governance, country, and industry controls. The questionnaire limits monitoring to the chain up to establishment output; it does not measure complete Scope 3 accounting or emissions reduction. Positive associations persist under alternative estimators and wild‐cluster inference. Customer requirements, environmental managers, and strategy strengthen the association under false‐discovery and family‐wise corrections. Practice‐index associations remain positive after excluding energy‐management content that may overlap with audit. The decomposition is consistent with the proposed monitoring pathway, while cross‐sectional timing and instrument strength warrant an associational interpretation. These findings clarify how external assessment relates to value‐chain information collection and reported environmental practices.

title: Financial Innovation and Sustainable Business Practices
summary: The connection between financial innovations and sustainable business, offers a framework that combines FinTech usage, green finance tools and sustainability performance. In the course of the research using a mixed methods methodology (systematic literature review and cross-sectoral case analysis), the key mechanisms for sustainable business models enabled by financial technologies including blockchain, artificial intelligence and digital platforms have been determined. In particular, the framework outlines three paths through which financial innovations help to ensure sustainable business development: resource efficiency improvement through digital finance tools, ESG integration through innovative financial instruments and stakeholders' value creation through inclusive financial models. The analysis of recent initiatives of industry players shows that companies which use innovations to achieve sustainable development are characterized by better access to green finance, higher level of transparency of supply chains and more robust stakeholder relations.

title: ESG DISCLOSURE PRACTICES AMONG EMERGING MARKET FIRMS: A CASE STUDY OF UZBEKISTAN
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure has become an important element of corporate transparency, sustainable development, and responsible business management. In emerging markets, ESG reporting plays a particularly significant role in attracting foreign investment, strengthening corporate governance, and improving companies’ competitiveness in international markets. This article examines ESG disclosure practices among firms operating in Uzbekistan, focusing on the development of sustainability reporting, regulatory frameworks, corporate transparency, and the challenges faced by local enterprises. The study highlights the growing importance of environmental responsibility, social accountability, and effective governance in Uzbekistan’s transition towards a sustainable market economy. It also explores the role of international ESG standards, including the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), in improving the quality and comparability of corporate disclosures. The findings suggest that although ESG awareness is increasing among Uzbek companies, significant improvements are still needed in data collection, reporting consistency, independent verification, and stakeholder engagement.

title: Value-based principles in sustainability reporting
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles have become a dominant framework for evaluating corporate sustainability. However, despite the widespread adoption of ESG, issues such as greenwashing, inconsistent accountability, persistent social and environmental injustices, and low trust remain unresolved. To address these gaps, this conceptual paper introduces a value-based ESG framework (V-ESG), which integrates 10 values—stewardship, accountability, leadership, transformation, compassion, justice, community wellbeing, integrity, trust and interconnectedness into ESG reporting. Through a multi-stakeholder engagement, we gathered diverse perspectives from selected participants from various sectors, including finance, energy, academia, policy, and social development to enhance the understanding process of this new reporting approach. An identification of recurring stakeholder perspectives and themes was conducted to prioritize core values, which were then mapped onto the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals to ensure alignment with global sustainability reporting framework. Additionally, a literature review reinforced the selection of values and development of measurement indicators for V-ESG implementation. The conceptual contribution suggests that values-driven sustainability may strengthen long-term institutional trust, corporate responsibility, and community impact. The framework could enhance traditional ESG by embedding ethical leadership, social justice, and governance transparency into sustainability strategies. By promoting a holistic, resilient, and adaptive approach, V-ESG could offer a robust alternative to traditional ESG, ensuring that businesses and investment practices not only comply with regulatory standards but also uphold ethical imperatives for a just and sustainable future. There is also a need to develop capacity of leaders and corporate teams in enhancing awareness and capability on V-ESG as a measurement tool for voluntary certification.

title: DETERMINANTS OF INVESTOR TRUST IN GREEN BONDS
summary: The importance of investor trust in ensuring that green bonds successfully mobilize funding for ecologically sustainable activities has increased due to the swift growth of green finance. However, the information and credibility mechanisms driving investor trust remain relatively understudied, especially in emerging markets. In the context of the Vietnamese market, this study aims to explore the relationship between investor trust in green bonds and Green Accounting Information Quality (GAIQ), Green Bond Disclosure Transparency (GBDT), External Review and Assurance (ERA), and Issuer ESG Reputation (IER). Using survey data from 369 ordinary investors and representatives of institutional investors, the study creates an integrated information-and-credibility paradigm based on information asymmetry and signaling viewpoints. The suggested relationships are evaluated using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). The results show that investor trust is positively and considerably impacted by all four focus variables, with ERA having the greatest impact, followed by GAIQ, GBDT, and IER. The model accounts for 50.1% of the variance in investor trust, suggesting that investor trust is influenced by a variety of information and credibility mechanisms rather than only green labeling. By combining firm-level green accounting data, bond-specific disclosure, independent assurance, and issuer ESG reputation under a single investor-trust framework, the study adds to the literature on green finance and accounting. The results are especially pertinent to investors assessing the quality of green bonds and the risk of greenwashing; listed companies and financial managers looking to bolster the credibility of green bonds; accounting and assurance professionals in charge of sustainability information and verification; and policymakers and regulators creating disclosure, assurance, and investor-protection mechanisms for Vietnam's developing green bond market. Overall, the study emphasizes how crucial it is to combine reliable external and reputational signals with high-quality information in order to boost investor trust and promote the long-term growth of green financing.

title: Digital Technology Adoption and Accounting Literacy in Financial Recording Practices: A Qualitative Case Study of a Rural Food Micro Small Medium Enterprise (MSME) in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia
summary: Financial recording is essential for improving the sustainability and financial management of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Previous studies have mainly focused on MSMEs that either lack financial records or adopt digital bookkeeping through formal training, while limited attention has been given to businesses that independently adopt digital recording technologies despite having limited accounting literacy. This study addresses this gap by examining the financial recording practices of 48 Salai Smoke House, a rural smoked-food MSME in Kampung Terachi, Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. Using a descriptive qualitative case study, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with the business owner and analysed thematically. The findings show that the enterprise uses a Point-of-Sale (POS) system as its primary recording tool, supported by manual verification of cash, QR (MAE/DuitNow), and bank transfer transactions, while maintaining a separate business bank account. Despite this level of digital technology adoption, financial records are not prepared within a structured accounting framework, and the owner has not received formal accounting or financial management training. These findings reveal a critical implementation gap between technology adoption and accounting literacy, indicating that digital tools alone are insufficient to strengthen financial reporting practices. This study contributes to the literature by providing evidence from an underexplored rural Malaysian context and highlights the importance of integrating digitalization initiatives with accounting literacy programmes to support the long-term sustainability of rural food MSMEs.

title: Financial sector of Ukraine: European integration through the prism of digitalisation, artificial intelligence, and innovative financial technologies
summary: Purpose: This paper examines the digital transformation of Ukraine’s financial sector through digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and financial technologies in the context of European integration. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study uses secondary data from the World Bank, International Monetary Fund, and National Bank of Ukraine for 2018–2024; the sample covers one country over seven years, with 24 annual indicators. Six analytical tables assess technological development, digital resilience, and regulatory harmonisation. The analysis is descriptive: it traces annual trends and examines how Ukrainian financial standards align with EU standards. Research Limitation: The analysis relies on secondary data and covers 2018–2024; its descriptive design does not identify causal effects or separate digitalisation from martial law and EU accession conditionality. Findings: The results show rapid movement toward a cashless economy and growing use of AI for risk management and cybersecurity. Despite geopolitical challenges, Ukraine has maintained digital transformation and harmonised more than 80% of relevant financial legislation with European Union (EU) standards, including PSD2 and DORA. Practical Implication: Digital technologies can strengthen financial resilience, risk management, and regulatory convergence. Social Implication: Responsible digitalisation can improve financial accessibility and transparency while supporting public trust. Originality/Value: Unlike single-channel studies of digital banking, AI law or public finance, the study examines 24 indicators in six groups together, showing that EU harmonisation kept its pre-war pace during the full-scale war while most digital indicators grew more slowly; it also highlights ethical AI governance as a condition for sustainable digital development.

title: Prioritizing and selecting the G-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry using a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach: BWM-TRUST
summary: Purpose: In today's turbulent and uncertain environment, organizations are compelled to revise traditional supply chain approaches and adopt strategies that simultaneously address environmental sustainability and resilience to disruptions. Accordingly, this study aims to develop a decision-making framework for evaluating and selecting green-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry—suppliers that demonstrate both strong environmental performance and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to disruptions. Methodology: This research employs a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework that integrates the Best-Worst Method (BWM) to determine the weights of evaluation criteria with the mulTi-noRmalization mUltiDistance aSsessmenT (TRUST) technique to rank suppliers as alternatives. The evaluation criteria, categorized into "green" and "resilience" dimensions, were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert input. These criteria include: waste generation, employee training, possession of eco-friendly certifications, pollution control initiatives, responsiveness, coordination, agility, information sharing, and efficient resource utilization. Data related to five real suppliers in the natural stone industry were collected through expert surveys and fed into the proposed evaluation model. Findings: The results revealed that "efficient resource utilization" holds the highest weight among the green and resilience criteria. Furthermore, based on the TRUST-based ranking, supplier A2 was identified as the top-performing green-resilient supplier. Originality/Value: The proposed model offers a practical, structured tool to help supply chain managers enhance sustainability and resilience amid growing environmental and operational disruptions.

title: Materiality and investor reaction to environmental corporate social responsibility : A replication and extension of Flammer (2013)
summary: Abstract Research Summary We replicate and extend Flammer's (2013) event study of investor reaction to environmental corporate social responsibility. Flammer found that investors react positively to eco‐friendly events and negatively to eco‐harmful events, with positive reactions diminishing and negative reactions intensifying from 1980 to 2009. We confirm her results in a narrow replication and find that these time trends persist in a quasi‐replication extending the sample through 2019, despite major shifts in the institutional environment for sustainability investing. We then extend Flammer by incorporating financial materiality and find that the investor reactions and time trends Flammer observed are primarily concentrated in material events. Notably, investors drew this distinction throughout the 40‐year window we study, predating the institutionalization of materiality‐based sustainability analysis. Managerial Summary We examine how investors respond to companies' environmental actions. Analyzing 40 years of data on US‐listed public firms, we find that investors reward companies for eco‐friendly actions and penalize them for harmful ones. Over time, these reactions have shifted: investors have grown less enthusiastic about eco‐friendly actions and more critical of harmful ones. Importantly, investors react primarily to environmental actions that are financially relevant, or “material,” to the business and were doing so well before formal standards existed. Within material actions, positive reactions to eco‐friendly initiatives have weakened while negative reactions to eco‐harmful ones have grown stronger. These findings suggest that managers should prioritize environmental initiatives closely tied to their company's financial performance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption, Governance Disclosure and Responsible Banking in Emerging Markets
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is spreading through emerging-market banking faster than the institutions meant to govern it, with consequences for responsible and sustainable finance. We hand-code eleven AI adoption and governance items on a graded 0–3 scale from annual reports of 143 listed commercial banks in eleven emerging markets over 2014–2025 (1582 bank-years), linking every positive score to a verbatim quotation, and merge the index with World Bank, governance and dated regulatory data. Adoption disclosure rises from 5.0% to 83.2% of banks, while governance disclosure reaches only 33.6%, and within banks, adoption trends upward 5.6 times faster (about 3–6 times across robustness tests). Governance disclosure accelerates only in 2024 and 2025, before most banking supervisors had issued any AI instrument and at least as strongly where none existed. Within countries, adoption tracks internet penetration and governance tracks the rule of law, though neither is robust to country-specific trends; data protection laws and national AI strategies explain neither series. Disclosed governance shows no association with credit risk or profitability, and the hypothesised link between adoption and capital ratios (H2) is not supported. The results identify a pre-institutional stage in which AI governance is neither demanded nor supplied, and offer a ready disclosure template.

title: Integration of Digital Business Processes and Financial Analysis in Modern International Business
summary: Purpose: To examine the impact of digital transformation on enterprise efficiency and financial performance and identify the key mechanisms through which digital technologies improve business process management in international companies. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employed a secondary statistical analysis of publicly available financial data from 100 large international companies in five sectors. The sample was compiled from the Fortune Global 500 and Forbes Global 2000 rankings. Comparative analysis and statistical testing were applied to evaluate differences in financial performance among firms with varying levels of digitalisation. Research Limitation: The analysis is limited to secondary financial data from large international companies. Survivorship and listing bias are possible, and differences are not adjusted for size, capital or sector. Future research should incorporate longitudinal and firm-level analyses. Findings: Companies with higher levels of digital integration demonstrated superior financial performance, including higher return on assets, return on equity, and revenue growth. Statistical testing confirmed significant differences in financial indicators between firms with different levels of digitalisation. Practical Implication: The findings support developing digital transformation strategies that improve business processes and financial management. Social Implication: Digital transformation may promote innovation, competitiveness, and sustainable organisational development. Originality/Value: The study provides empirical evidence linking digital integration with enterprise financial performance and measures integration by how many of the four management systems a firm has implemented, rather than by one or two systems.

title: Competing narratives and the politics of tourism restriction in the 1000 visitor per day quota policy in Komodo National Park
summary: The 1000-visitor-per-day restriction policy in Komodo National Park (Indonesia) represents a contested form of environmental governance shaped by competing ecological and socioeconomic interests. Despite its policy relevance, public responses and stakeholder perspectives surrounding the policy remain underexplored. This study examines public sentiment and stakeholder perspectives using a qualitative multi-source approach based on 264 Facebook comments, 69 online news articles, policy documents, and nine semi-structured interviews. Facebook comments were manually classified into four sentiment categories to assess public responses to the policy, while online news articles, interview transcripts, and policy documents were analyzed thematically using NVivo 15 software. Findings reveal divergent public responses and stakeholder perspectives, with conservation-oriented narratives emphasizing ecosystem protection and socioeconomic narratives highlighting livelihood impacts, economic uncertainty, and distributive concerns among tourism-dependent communities. The findings further indicate that the policy influences regional tourism dynamics by redistributing visitor flows toward surrounding destinations, particularly Labuan Bajo. The study demonstrates that visitor-restriction policies can become arenas of governance contestation, shaping tourism systems and stakeholder relations. It contributes to the literature on environmental governance and tourism management by highlighting the socio-political tensions embedded in restrictive tourism policies and the importance of inclusive governance approaches in protected areas.

title: The Impact of Business Environmental Changes on the Adoption of a Strategic Pivot: A Case Study of Zar Industrial Group
summary: Objective: This study aimed to examine the impact of business environmental changes on strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group and develop a conceptual model of this process. Methods and Materials: This applied qualitative study used a grounded theory design. The study population consisted of Zar Industrial Group managers and university professors with expertise in strategic management and organizational change. Participants were selected purposively based on their knowledge and professional experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers of the holding company and its food-industry subsidiaries, together with academic experts. Interviews continued until theoretical saturation, resulting in a final sample of 12 participants. Interview transcripts were systematically coded, compared, and categorized to identify the principal dimensions and mechanisms associated with strategic pivot adoption. Findings: The analysis produced seven main categories and 41 related concepts. The categories included macro-environmental changes and external pressures; risk, uncertainty, and financial pressure; supply-chain and operational disruptions; market-oriented and commercial responses; structural and business-model redesign; innovation, technology, and digital transformation; and human capital, organizational learning, and institutionalization of the strategic pivot. Environmental turbulence generated financial, operational, and market pressures that stimulated coordinated strategic responses. These responses involved market reorientation, business-model redesign, technological innovation, digital transformation, and capability development. Human capital and organizational learning played a central role in sustaining and institutionalizing the strategic pivot. Conclusion: Strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group represents a multidimensional organizational response to environmental uncertainty rather than an isolated managerial decision. Successful pivots require alignment among market responses, structural transformation, technological innovation, operational resilience, and organizational learning. The proposed conceptual model can help managers recognize environmental signals, coordinate adaptive actions, and strengthen organizational resilience and long-term competitiveness.

title: Climate Change and Its Impact on Global Politics
summary: Abstract: Climate is the average weather of an area. Climate refers to the long- term pattern of weather conditions in a particular place or region, usually measured over a period of thirty years or more. It includes factors such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, and atmospheric pressure. Climate change has emerged as one of the most significant challenges to contemporary global politics. Climate change refers to long-term changes in the Earth’s temperature, rainfall, wind patterns, and other climatic conditions. Today, the major cause of rapid climate change is the increase in greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide largely due to human activities. Its impacts extend beyond environmental concerns, influencing international relations, economic security, and global governance. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events, sea-level rise, and increasing pressure on natural resources have created new challenges for states and international institutions. Climate change has also intensified debates between developed and developing countries concerning historical responsibility, climate finance, technology transfer and equitable burden-sharing. International agreements such as the Paris Agreement demonstrate the importance of multilateral cooperation, while differences in national interests often complicate collective action. Furthermore, climate related displacement and competition over scarce resources may contribute to social and political instability in vulnerable regions. This paper examines the relationship between climate change and global politics, focusing on its influence on international cooperation, geopolitical relations, security, and sustainable development. It argues that addressing climate change requires stronger multilateral institutions, equitable international cooperation, and policies that integrate environmental sustainability with global peace and development.

summary: France’s strategic posture combines a permanent UN Security Council seat, an independent nuclear deterrent, and dispersed overseas territories, making it a revealing case for examining how structural dependencies interact with a broad set of strategic responsibilities. title: The Institutionalization of REIT Sustainability Reporting: Cross‐Country Evidence From ESG Disclosure Regimes and Building Sustainability Policies
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the institutionalization and textual evolution of sustainability reporting among listed real estate investment trusts (REITs) in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, and Japan between 2020 and 2025. Reporting is framed as the joint product of two institutional layers: capital‐market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure regimes and building‐level sustainability policies. For the full listed universe (641 REIT‐year observations), the analysis combines transition modeling with binomial logit estimation. To analyze the text of 307 hand‐collected reports, it applies term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF–IDF) comparison, Structural Topic Modeling, and a human‐validated building‐level sustainability keyword index. The share of listed REITs issuing an identifiable sustainability report rose from 43.1% to 63.9%; new adoption (26.4%) far outpaced discontinuation (5.1%). Reporting language shifted toward structured, climate‐oriented, and implementation‐focused content. Asset‐level sustainability vocabulary is densest where building‐level instruments are longest established and rose fastest where those instruments expanded. The two layers leave distinguishable traces: disclosure regimes most visibly on the issuance margin, building policies on the content margin. The proposed index offers a transferable starting point for monitoring asset‐level sustainability language in corporate disclosure.

title: How Digital-Intelligence Integration Enhances Energy Resilience: A Mixed-Methods Study
summary: Against the backdrop of green and low-carbon development and growing risks to energy systems, enhancing energy resilience helps ensure energy security, maintain the stable operation of energy systems, and support their sustainable development. Based on panel data from 30 provinces in China from 2015 to 2023, this study employs a mixed-method approach combining multiple linear regression and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to examine the impact effects and configurational paths of digital-intelligence integration on energy resilience. The results show that (1) compared with digitalization or intelligence alone, digital-intelligence integration significantly enhances energy resilience; (2) digital-intelligence integration can improve energy resilience by promoting dual green innovation and financial development; (3) informal environmental regulation plays a positive moderating role, whereas formal environmental regulation shows no significant moderating effect; and (4) further fsQCA analysis reveals that the improvement of energy resilience depends on the coordinated configuration of multiple factors, and different regions can achieve enhancement through differentiated combinations of conditions. These findings offer empirical evidence and theoretical support for local tailored adoption of digital-intelligence integration to improve energy resilience and promote the sustainable development of energy systems.

title: Application of Blockchain Technology in Agricultural Product Traceability
summary: In today's world, people's living standards have been gradually improving, and their health awareness has been constantly increasing; consumers need better quality and experience when shopping. The process of selling agricultural products needs to be further developed with digital transformation. The construction of an agricultural product traceability system based on blockchain technology enables full process tracking of the agricultural product supply chain for the integrity and transparency of traceability information; furthermore, because of its decentralized feature and immutability of transaction records, it provides a novel way for transforming and upgrading traditional agricultural product retail processes. In order to make clear the direction of this field, we attempt to summarize and review the existing domestic and international literature within the scope of blockchain technology and agricultural product sales: analyze the current research status, theoretical foundation of blockchain tech, case study and analysis as well as policy support, identify the shortcoming in current academic research (sample, method, depth, scenario).In doing so, it aims to clarify the research context and development status of the field, organize mainstream research perspectives, key technologies, and typical applications, analyze existing deficiencies and controversial issues, and thereby provide a forecast for future research directions. This offers theoretical references and insights for subsequent studies, promoting further deepening and improvement of related research.

title: Algorithmic Bias Concerns and Acceptance of AI Supported Legal Decision Making in Bangladesh
summary: Artificial intelligence can assist legal work while creating risks of discrimination, opaque reasoning and diminished accountability. This study examines whether concern about biased training data coexists with perceived usefulness and support for safeguards among respondents to a Bangladesh legal-AI survey. The analysis uses 385 adult, AI-aware survey records supplied by the research team. Because the questionnaire combines risk perceptions, utility and governance preferences, the analysis retains individual items rather than presenting the blocks as validated scales. Descriptive distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and exploratory Spearman correlations assess distinct aspects of the research question. Concern about biased training data was endorsed by 334 respondents (86.8%), regular audits by 317 (82.3%) and a right to review or appeal by 328 (85.2%). AI assistance with organising information was endorsed by 247 (64.2%); 219 (56.9%) endorsed both this usefulness item and bias concern. The rank correlation between bias concern and perceived usefulness was small (ρ = .075), with no clear evidence of association after adjustment for multiple comparisons. These self-reported attitudes cannot establish the fairness of a system, causal effects or the actual conditions under which a respondent would rely on an AI recommendation. The results point to the importance of measuring perceived benefits, risk and procedural protections separately. The article integrates technology acceptance and procedural justice as a framework for future scenario-based studies and proposes proportionate auditing, meaningful human review and accessible contestation for legal decision support. title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE MODERATING GREEN INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL AND BLUE ACCOUNTING DISCLOSURE EFFECTS ON SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE
summary: This study aimed to examine and analyze the role of corporate governance in moderating the influence of green intellectual capital and blue accounting disclosure on corporate sustainability performance. The study employed an associative quantitative approach. The population consisted of 91 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2024 period, and a sample of 21 companies was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 105 firm-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and corporate governance reports. The data were analyzed using panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis with the assistance of EViews 13 software after descriptive statistics, model selection tests, and classical assumption tests were conducted. The results showed that green intellectual capital had no significant effect on sustainability performance, with a t-statistic of -1.855511 and a significance value of 0.0664. Blue accounting disclosure had a positive and significant effect on sustainability performance, with a t-statistic of 2.685552 and a significance value of 0.0085. Corporate governance significantly moderated the influence of green intellectual capital on sustainability performance, with a t-statistic of 2.044847 and a significance value of 0.0442. However, corporate governance did not moderate the influence of blue accounting disclosure on sustainability performance, with a t-statistic of -1.407638 and a significance value of 0.1632. These findings implied that environmentally oriented intangible resources alone were insufficient to enhance sustainability performance, while greater transparency in water and marine resource management improved sustainability performance, and effective governance enabled firms to better utilize green intellectual resources to achieve sustainability objectives.

title: STATE POLICY ON BANKING REGULATION AMID THE DEVELOPMENT OF FINTECH TECHNOLOGIES AND GROWING DIGITAL RISKS TO NATIONAL SECURITY
summary: The purpose of the study is to examine the transformation of state regulation of banking activities in Ukraine in the context of the development of FinTech technologies and the intensification of digital risks, as well as to substantiate directions for improving the regulatory framework and banking supervision mechanisms, taking into account the requirements of financial stability and national security. The article substantiates that the digital transformation of the financial sector causes the modernization of banking services, contributes to increasing the efficiency of financial intermediation, expands financial inclusion, and ensures the development of innovative business models; however, it generates new challenges for the system of state regulation of banking activities, ensuring financial stability and cybersecurity. The principal trends in the digitalization of banking activities are identified, and the impact of FinTech technologies on the transformation of state regulatory mechanisms in the financial sector is characterized. The performance of Ukraine’s major banks — PrivatBank, Oschadbank, and Raiffeisen Bank — during 2022–2025 is analyzed, revealing growing trends toward the digitalization of banking operations, the expansion of remote service channels, an increase in the number of users of digital services, and a strengthening role of financial technologies in ensuring the competitiveness of banking institutions. It is established that, alongside the positive effects of digital transformation, cyber risks, digital fraud, data leakage, technological dependence on external platforms, and other threats affecting national security are increasing. The need to improve state banking regulation is substantiated through the development of RegTech and SupTech technologies, the introduction of risk-based digital supervision, stronger cyber resilience of banking infrastructure, improved digital-risk management mechanisms, and the harmonization of national legislation with European standards of digital financial regulation. It is demonstrated that an effective combination of innovative development in the financial sector and modern mechanisms of state oversight is a necessary prerequisite for ensuring financial stability and protecting national interests in the digital economy.

title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
summary: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

title: Smart Loan and Asset Management System with Automated Notification and Redemption Tracking for Sulu Padjak
summary: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a Smart Loan and Asset Management System with Automated Notification and Redemption Tracking for Sulu M'C Chay Padjak in Jolo, Sulu, Philippines, addressing inefficiencies in manual recordkeeping, financial computations, inventory monitoring, and customer communication. Guided by the Input–Process–Output (IPO) model, the study employed the Waterfall Software Development Life Cycle, comprising requirements analysis, system design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with the pawnshop manager and two cashiers, document reviews, and user acceptance evaluation involving the owner and personnel. The locally hosted web-based system integrated customer management, pawn transactions, automated loan computations, redemption and forfeiture tracking, inventory monitoring, financial reporting, role-based access controls, audit logging, and SMS notifications. Testing achieved 85% code coverage of critical business functions, with search and dashboard responses completed in less than two seconds and ticket generation in less than three seconds after data entry, compared with the reported 10–15-minute manual transaction cycle. User acceptance evaluation yielded an overall mean of 4.50, interpreted as Excellent. The study concluded that the system achieved its intended objectives and recommended its operational adoption, regular system maintenance, and future enhancements involving mobile accessibility and electronic payment integration. The project supports Sustainable Development Goals 8, 9, 10, and 16 by promoting operational efficiency, technological innovation, accessible financial services, and accountable information management. Its sustainability contribution lies in strengthening the economic, technological, and institutional capacity of a community-based financial service provider through improved transaction accuracy, service reliability, and operational transparency.

title: The Transformation of Strategic Management in The Digital Age: The Impact of Digital Platforms and Data Analytics
summary: Purpose: The purpose of the study is to identify the transformation of strategic management in the digital age under the influence of digital platforms and data analytics in the platform economy. Design/Methodology/Approach: The methodological basis of the study is documentary analysis of more than 30 consulting reports and industry reviews for 2024–2025 and statistical materials of international organisations, selected using inclusion criteria and covering 300 organisations as units of analysis. Declared and actual digital practices were recorded separately; descriptive statistics summarised the indicators, and bivariate correlations linked data analytics use, platform integration, review adaptability and security integration. Research Limitation: The study is based on documentary analysis and aggregated secondary data, so its results show prevalence and association, not causation. Findings: Digital platforms and data analytics are becoming the environment, not auxiliary tools, for strategic decision-making. There is a shift from long-term planning to frequent, highly adaptive, data-based reviews. Hierarchical control weakens as platform rules, metrics and architectural constraints gain weight. Declared priorities exceed actual integration, and data analytics use, platform integration and review adaptability correlate moderately. Information security emerges as a strategic factor in selecting initiatives and limiting platform scaling. Practical Implication: The results can inform more adaptive and coordinated approaches to strategic management in the digital economy. Social Implication: The new coordination mechanisms change how work is organised, including more decentralised decision-making, cross-functional collaboration, and remote or platform-mediated work. These changes alter job roles, workplace relationships and employee expectations, so they need to be managed inclusively and with attention to job quality and wellbeing. Originality/Value: Prior studies examine platforms, data analytics and security largely in parallel, leaving the strategic level of digital transformation under-conceptualised. The study links them within one strategy cycle, separating declared from actual use and showing where control moves when hierarchy weakens.

title: Assessing the Interaction Mechanisms and Multiscale Spatial Dynamic Effect of the Economy–Land–Ecological Environment System on the Loess Plateau of China
summary: Abstract The Loess Plateau is a representative loess accumulation area in China, and the coordinated development of its cities is particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change threats. This research develops the economy–land–ecological environment (ELE) system to quantify the coordinated development status through the coupling coordination degree (CCD) model and applies the multiscale geographically weighted regression model to reveal spatial dynamic effects of key driving factors. Based on the analysis, the results indicate that the overall CCD is at a moderate level, with the Ordos Plateau showing a high CCD level and the Longzhong Plateau a low CCD level. Second, the more developed a city, the higher the CCD value. Third, there is a significant spatial autocorrelation of CCD in the Loess Plateau, and the northern region of the Loess Plateau exhibits a high–high clustering pattern. Finally, there is substantial spatial nonstationarity among driving factors. Specifically, industrial structure, urbanization, foreign direct investment, and industrialization tend to facilitate coordinated development. Technological innovation and environmental governance gradually reduce their inhibiting effects and shift toward a promoting role. The constraining impact of population density becomes increasingly prominent. The ELE framework and the multiscale spatial analysis proposed in this study provide urban planners in other ecologically fragile regions with a general tool to identify key development constraints, set priorities for governance objectives, and design refined and sustainable urban development plans.

title: A Quantitative Framework for Assessing Digital Sovereignty
summary: Digital sovereignty is a political buzzword. However, there are diverging views on how to define and measure it. Throughout this study we propose the creation of a quantitative framework to measure digital sovereignty capabilities on a country's performance in three key areas: technology, government, and users. Through our analysis covering 123 countries, we have shown the different paths towards achieving sovereignty that are imprinted into how the countries contribute to the digital economy and reflect the asymmetries existing in the global value chains. The US and China both show a strong technological leadership, especially regarding emerging technologies, while the EU maintains a balance between innovation and regulations that the new strategies and MFF must address in order to become a relevant global player.

title: Economic Sustainability as a Factor of Resilience of Economic Systems in the Crisis-Digital Paradigm of Sustainable Development Management
summary: Purpose: To examine the relationship between economic sustainability, innovation, and sustainable development as key determinants of the resilience of modern economic systems and identify strategic approaches for strengthening resilience through digital transformation. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employed a qualitative research design based on a systematic review of scientific literature, comparative analysis, and conceptual synthesis. The review covered 31 studies (2020–2026) retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, supplemented by Google Scholar, and identified the principal mechanisms that enhance the adaptability and long-term stability of economic systems. Research Limitation: The study is conceptual and based on secondary sources. Future research should validate the proposed framework using empirical evidence from different sectors. Findings: The results show that economic sustainability is closely linked to integrating technological and digital innovations into production and management processes. Structural adaptability, system integration, stakeholder participation, human capital development, and effective resource management were identified as key prerequisites for sustainable growth and resilience. Automation, digitalisation, and artificial intelligence improve business processes, increase operational efficiency, and support sustainable development by integrating economic, environmental, and social objectives. Practical Implication: The findings guide policymakers and business leaders in designing innovation-driven strategies that enhance economic resilience. Social Implication: Strengthening economic sustainability promotes long-term stability, social well-being, environmental responsibility, and resilience. Originality/Value: The study integrates the established constructs of economic sustainability, innovation, digital transformation, and resilience into one framework; what is new is the crisis-digital paradigm, which treats digital tools as a system-forming element of resilience management.

title: A Study on The Evolving Financial Landscape, Risk Dynamics and Institutional Integration of Cryptocurrency in India
summary: Abstract The rapid development of cryptocurrency and blockchain technology has significantly influenced the global financial landscape, creating new opportunities for digital financial innovation while introducing various financial, technological, and regulatory challenges. This study examines the evolving financial landscape of cryptocurrency in India, with particular emphasis on risk dynamics and institutional integration. It explores the development of Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs), the major risks associated with cryptocurrency, and the regulatory mechanisms introduced by the Government of India and financial authorities. The study focuses on market volatility, cybersecurity threats, consumer protection, money laundering, financial stability, taxation, and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) compliance. It also examines the growing relationship between cryptocurrency-related activities, financial institutions, fintech organisations, and India's broader digital-finance ecosystem. The research adopts a secondary and descriptive analytical approach based on publications from the Reserve Bank of India, the Income Tax Department, the Financial Intelligence Unit–India, the Bank for International Settlements, and other credible sources. The study highlights the importance of balancing technological innovation with effective regulation, risk management, and consumer protection. It concludes that a transparent and well-structured regulatory framework is essential for addressing cryptocurrency-related risks and supporting the responsible development of India's digital financial ecosystem.

title: A Paradox of ‘Sustainable’ Tobacco Business: Rethinking Sustainability Reporting from Ethics and Public Health Perspectives
summary: Abstract Public health recognizes that businesses significantly shape people’s health and health inequities. Over time, businesses have been increasingly asked to make disclosures about their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) impacts. India mandates the top 1000 listed companies by market capitalization to submit business responsibility and sustainability reports. In this context, we discuss how the tobacco industry, which causes significant health and environmental harms, ought to be seen as distinct from many other businesses. We demonstrate three problematic aspects of how tobacco companies are reporting on sustainability: (1) their reporting creates a false impression of them being ‘responsible’ businesses, (2) they routinely underplay the ESG impacts of tobacco products and processes, and (3) the current reporting does not capture compliance with tobacco sector-specific regulatory requirements. We recommend that tobacco companies—as solo or conglomerate businesses—should be mandated to use a tobacco sector-specific template, developed by the regulator with no influence from the tobacco sector, that includes tobacco-specific ESG and health impacts as well as tobacco-specific regulatory compliance. We suggest that the proposed ESG rating shall either exclude the tobacco industry or rate it alongside other ‘harm/extractive’ industries. It shall not be allowed to use such reports for publicity gains.

title: Sinergi Human Capital 5.0 dan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pengambilan Keputusan Bisnis untuk Meningkatkan Daya Saing UMKM di Era Ekonomi Digital
summary: Synergy of Human Capital 5.0 and Artificial Intelligence in Business Decision-Making to Enhance MSME Competitiveness in the Digital Economy Era. The digital economy and the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are changing how micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) make decisions and which skills they need. However, AI adoption does not automatically improve competitiveness because it depends on the readiness of people and management. This article aims to (1) analyze how AI disruption and automation reshape competence requirements in MSMEs, (2) examine the role of Human Capital 5.0 in using AI for business decisions, (3) identify opportunities, challenges, and the roles of management and education in human–AI synergy, and (4) formulate a conceptual framework of that synergy. The study is a structured qualitative literature review of 29 sources published in 2022–2026, consisting of international and national journal articles, the author’s earlier studies, and reports from international and government institutions, analyzed through thematic synthesis. The review shows that the literature mostly addresses AI adoption from technological and organizational angles, while human competence as a determinant of decision quality has not been fully integrated. Human Capital 5.0 functions as the ability to interpret, test, and control AI outputs, whereas AI extends data-processing and prediction capacity. Management shapes this synergy through leadership, human resource development, and responsible AI governance, while education supplies competencies and collaboration with MSMEs. The article proposes a five-stage conceptual model supported by leadership, digital readiness, data quality, technology access, and ethics, together with four propositions for future empirical testing. The model remains propositional and requires empirical validation. Strengthening MSMEs therefore requires combining AI literacy training, mentoring, cross-sector collaboration, and responsible AI governance.

summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the effect of good corporate governance mechanism, financial performance, growth opportunity, and ESG disclosure on firm value. The independent variables used in this study are managerial ownership, institutional ownership, profitability, leverage, growth opportunity, and ESG disclosure. Meanwhile, the dependent variable used in this study is firm value. In addition, the control variable used in this study is firm size. The population in this study consists of companies listed in the IDX30 index on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2022-2024 period. The sampling technique used is saturation sampling technique, therefore, the total sample used in this study is 90 samples. The data used are secondary data obtained from the annual reports and sustainability reports of IDX30 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The analysis method used in this study is panel data regression analysis using the EViews 13 software. The result of this study show that leverage, ESG disclosure, and firm size have an effect on firm value. Meanwhile, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, profitability, and growth opportunity do not have an effect on firm value.

title: Rural food markets and their implications for the availability and affordability of nutrient-dense foods in Bihar, India
summary: The adequate consumption of nutrient-dense foods such as fruits, vegetables, and animal-source foods is crucial for achieving good health. However, in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), consumption of nutrient-dense foods is extremely low. Food markets are a critical node in the rural food environments of LMICs. Yet, they remain understudied and there is little granular information available on how well-equipped they are to supply affordable nutrient-dense foods. We address this gap in knowledge by contributing information on rural food markets from Bihar, India. We use a primary market survey conducted in two districts of Bihar, and examine how market infrastructure, governance, and spatial organisation shape the availability and prices of nutrient-dense foods. By applying agglomerative hierarchical clustering, we identify three market types and link the market typology with information from a separate primary survey of food prices to ask whether prices of nutrient-dense foods differ by market type. There are three main findings of our study: (i) There is a near universal and extreme lack of market infrastructure relevant to making safe and affordable nutrient-dense foods available. (ii) Market types differ largely by size and proximity to the nearest urban centre but display remarkably little difference in infrastructure and governance. (iii) Availability of nutrient-dense foods is lower in remote rural markets, but prices in these markets are not consistently higher than in larger, more urban markets. Our findings highlight that modest infrastructure investments, standardised management practices, and promotion of a diverse mix of long and short supply chains could enhance access to nutrient-dense foods to address nutrition challenges in similar contexts of rural LMICs.

title: Digital Leadership, Change Readiness, And Technology-Enabled Organizational Performance
summary: The rapid advancement of digital technology necessitates organizational adaptation, yet digital leadership alone is insufficient to guarantee successful transformation. Internal factors, specifically change readiness, are crucial for effective technology adoption. This study investigates how digital leadership affects technology-enabled organizational performance, both directly and indirectly, through the mediating role of change readiness. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional survey approach, data were collected from 250 operational employees and middle managers across various sectors undergoing digital transformation. The conceptual model was evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS. The results indicate that digital leadership positively and significantly affects organizational change readiness and performance. Furthermore, change readiness significantly affects performance and serves as a complementary mediator between digital leadership and technology-enabled organizational performance. The structural model explains 55.4% of the variance in change readiness and 57.6% of the variance in organizational performance. Ultimately, this study concludes that effective digital leaders must proactively build collective organizational readiness to maximize the benefits of digital transformation initiatives.
