title: Generation Z's scepticism towards corporate socially responsible initiatives: insights from the UK market
summary: Purpose The study investigates Generation Z's scepticism towards socially responsible business practices, an underexplored dimension of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and identifies factors that contribute to such scepticism within the UK context. Design/methodology/approach The study adopted a qualitative approach using semi-structured interviews with thirty-five Gen Z consumers in the United Kingdom. The data were analysed using thematic analysis. Findings The findings reveal three categories of trust-building signals that shape consumers' sceptical responses: information-related signals, brand and retailer-related signals and fit and value-related signals. They further suggest that CSR scepticism encompasses scepticism towards CSR practices and CSR communication. In addition, consumers differed in the degree of CSR scepticism they exhibited, reflected in the motives they attributed to brands and retailers and the evidence they required before forming trust judgements. Differences in evidential requirements reflect the use of heuristic and systematic information processing. Practical implications The study offers guidance for brands and retailers in terms of implementing and communicating CSR practices to avoid consumer scepticism. It also implies the role of policymakers in helping consumers feel more confident in the credibility of CSR claims while supporting brands and retailers in reducing scepticism. Originality/value The study extends CSR scepticism literature by examining brands and retailers' socially responsible business practices and conceptualising CSR scepticism as an evaluative, overarching multidimensional construct. It further suggests that variation in CSR scepticism is reflected in consumers' evidential requirements and motive attributions and develops a conceptual framework integrating these insights.

title: Relationship Between Organizational Culture and Workplace Mobbing: A Critical and Comprehensive Review
summary: Workplace mobbing has become one of the most damaging and psychologically destructive problems in modern organizational life. Yet the cultural conditions within organizations that create and sustain this phenomenon remain surprisingly underexplored. This article offers a theoretically grounded, critically minded review of the relationship between organizational culture and workplace mobbing, drawing on peer-reviewed literature published between 1990 and 2025. The study examines how specific cultural features—including power distance, hierarchical structures, organizational silence, ethical leadership, inclusive management, psychological safety, and corporate social responsibility—either create fertile ground for mobbing or help prevent it. The analysis reveals a striking point: the relationship between culture and mobbing is not simply a correlation. It is constitutive and runs in both directions. Toxic, hierarchical, and authoritarian organizational cultures create the conditions for mobbing to take root and flourish, while mobbing itself gradually corrodes the culture around it, producing a self-reinforcing downward spiral of dysfunction. At the same time, organizations that build ethical, participatory, inclusive, and transparent cultures tend to protect their people from mobbing. This review contributes to knowledge by synthesizing empirical findings across multiple sectors, offering critical commentary on the theoretical and methodological weaknesses in existing research, and proposing an integrative framework that connects cultural antecedents to mobbing outcomes. The article concludes with practical, evidence-based recommendations for organizational leaders, human resources professionals, and policymakers seeking to address workplace mobbing through genuine cultural transformation—not superficial policy change.

title: THE EVOLVING LANDSCAPE OF DIGITAL LEADERSHIP IN THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
summary: Purpose Digital leadership is increasingly recognised as important for navigating digital transformation in the built environment, yet the knowledge base remains fragmented and conceptually dispersed. This study aims to examine the evolution, intellectual structure and emerging themes of digital leadership research in the built environment and identify directions for future research. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 154 peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus and IEEE Xplore and published between 2016 and 2026. VOSviewer was used to analyse publication trends, authorship, geographical distribution, sources and keyword co-occurrence to identify the intellectual and thematic structure of the field. Findings The findings indicate sustained growth in digital leadership research, particularly since 2022, although scholarly activity remains concentrated among a limited number of authors, countries and institutions. Five interconnected themes emerged: digital leadership and innovation; digital transformation and sustainability; leadership approaches and technological integration; digitalisation in construction; and organisational and information management. The thematic evolution indicates a shift from foundational discussions towards competency, implementation and performance-oriented research. Originality/value The study consolidates the fragmented literature and provides a focused map of the evolving intellectual and thematic landscape of digital leadership in the built environment. It further identifies conceptual, contextual and empirical gaps and proposes directions for developing more context-sensitive digital leadership research and frameworks.

title: UNDERSTANDING GOING CONCERN AUDIT OPINION: AUDIT QUALITY, SIZE, AND GOVERNANCE EFFECTS
summary: This study aimed to examine the effect of audit quality, firm size, and Good Corporate Governance mechanisms on going concern audit opinions in food and beverage manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2017–2023 period. The study employed a quantitative approach with an associative-causal design. The population consisted of 83 food and beverage manufacturing companies, and a sample of 51 companies was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 357 observations over seven years. Secondary data were collected from financial statements, audit reports, and annual reports. The data were analyzed using logistic regression. The results showed that audit quality had a significant positive effect on going concern audit opinions, with a regression coefficient of 1.220 and a significance value of 0.000. Firm size had a significant negative effect on going concern audit opinions, with a regression coefficient of −0.340 and a significance value of 0.000. Good Corporate Governance had a significant positive effect on going concern audit opinions, with a regression coefficient of 3.016 and a significance value of 0.017. The logistic regression model explained 58.5 percent of the variation in going concern audit opinions, as indicated by the Nagelkerke R Square value, while the remaining 41.5 percent was attributed to factors outside the model. These findings implied that higher audit quality and stronger governance practices increased the likelihood of auditors disclosing going concern uncertainties, while larger firms were less likely to receive such opinions due to their stronger financial capacity and business sustainability.

title: Smart Contracts in the Private Law System: A Strategy for Overcoming Normative Uncertainty and Regulatory Prospects in Ukraine
summary: Digital transformation and the implementation of distributed ledger technologies define contemporary trends in the development of private law, necessitating the formation of an appropriate legal environment capable of ensuring the efficiency of innovation by regulating the behavior of subjects within the digital space. Given that Ukraine is currently a global leader in blockchain technology adoption, this work represents an attempt to define the directions for adapting Ukrainian contract law to the challenges of algorithmization and automation. This article analyzes the impact of digital transformation on the fundamental institutions of Ukrainian contract law, using smart contracts as a primary element of blockchain technology. Research into the nature of smart contracts allows for the differentiation of the "smart legal contract" category, where contractual obligations are executed automatically by computer code. Based on a synthesis of technological understanding, practical implications (notably The DAO and Venus Protocol cases), and civil law theory, the work explores the deterministic nature of smart contracts (automatism, immutability, uniqueness) and examines their interaction with established categories such as party autonomy, good faith, and equivalence. Furthermore, the article applies a comparative analysis of three global regulatory strategies (analogy, radical restructuring through Lex Cryptographia, and moderate integration), involving international concepts from R. Crootof, B.J. Ard, G. Jaccard, and the ELI Principles on Blockchain Technology, Smart Contracts and Consumer Protection. Accordingly, it is concluded that the current stage of Ukrainian civil law development is characterized by the absence of a comprehensive legal infrastructure for smart contracts, leading to uncertainty regarding their legal nature and consequences. Under the influence of algorithmic determinism, traditional mechanisms of flexible regulation—such as contextual interpretation of contractual terms and retrospective adjustment of obligations in cases of changed circumstances or technical errors—lose their distinctiveness. This research proposes a comprehensive "roadmap" of reforms—from the adaptation of the Civil Code of Ukraine to the legalization of "expert oracle" mechanisms—aiming to facilitate further legal discussions on overcoming legal uncertainty and establishing Ukraine as one of the most progressive jurisdictions for digital innovation.

title: Government Failure and Corporate Reform
summary: Corporate law has been racked by a decades-long debate. Shareholder primacy theorists suggest that corporate leaders should focus exclusively on maximizing financial returns to shareholders, while stakeholder governance theorists suggest that corporate leaders should consider a broader range of concerns such as impacts on workers and the environment. Though the battle has been fought intensely on many fronts for years, there is one area of apparent agreement. Most commentators view stakeholder governance as a kind of second-best regulation. Ideally, the government would tend to worker and environmental concerns through real regulations, imposing financial penalties on corporations that behave in socially destructive ways. Corporate leaders could then focus on financial returns, given the knowledge that bad behavior would not be profitable. It is only when the government fails in its basic task by refusing to issue or enforce necessary regulations that it becomes necessary for corporations to balance different concerns internally. But although it seems to be a point of broad agreement, the idea that stakeholder governance is a response to government failure is incomplete. This Article unpacks that claim and reveals its shortcomings. It is far from obvious whether the government’s refusal to regulate in a space is a failure or simply a result of the democratic process given widespread disagreement. And even an “ideal” government would face limitations in its ability to drive good outcomes. Statutes and regulations are inherently limited tools, and there are many areas such as speech and dignitary interests where the government cannot interfere or provide an adequate solution. Understanding these shortcomings deepens the analysis of the relationship between corporate governance and the political process and reveals fresh insights about the debate between shareholder primacy and stakeholder governance.

title: Building Resilient Productivity in an Urban District Municipality through Disruptive Technology: A Case Study of Emfuleni Local Municipality, Vanderbijlpark, South Africa
summary: Abstract Urban municipalities face growing pressure to maintain service delivery amid technological change, population growth, rising costs and recurring disruptions. This study examines the role of disruptive technology in strengthening resilient productivity at Emfuleni Local Municipality (ELM) in Vanderbijlpark, South Africa. A qualitative case-study design was employed, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 10 senior municipal managers and desktop research. The study found that disruptive technology may function as an additional factor of production by helping municipalities respond to future labour shortages and productivity constraints. Participants also associated technology with more accurate data processing, fewer administrative errors, opportunities for citizen participation and the automation of repetitive tasks. However, they identified concerns about potential threats to skilled employment, employee readiness, privacy and the management of electronic records. The study recommends that municipal authorities develop clear technology-adoption roadmaps, strengthen legal and policy frameworks, improve electricity and communications infrastructure, invest in workforce reskilling and involve employees in change processes from an early stage. The findings offer a context-specific account of perceived opportunities and challenges at ELM. Given the single-case design, small purposive sample and 2021 data-collection period, the findings should not be interpreted as statistically representative of other municipalities. Keywords: disruptive technology; municipal productivity; organisational resilience; local government; digital transformation; public service delivery; Emfuleni Local Municipality

title: Enterprise Risk Management Culture and Implementation Challenges: Exploratory Evidence from Five African Countries
summary: This study evaluates the enterprise risk management (ERM) culture and implementation practices within public, parastatal, and private-sector organizations in five African countries (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Nigeria). Utilizing an exploratory, multi-country convenience survey of 35 senior organizational executives (N = 35) alongside a systematic review of corporate governance literature, the paper examines key drivers of risk culture maturity and operational effectiveness. The empirical findings reveal that while functional awareness of risk assessment is universally high (100%), formal risk management culture remains underdeveloped due to unarticulated risk philosophies, vague risk appetites, and fragmented risk communication. Furthermore, implementation effectiveness is substantially constrained by insufficient technical capacity, weak monitoring infrastructures, absent post-mitigation review mechanisms, and limited board-level sponsorship. The paper presents a structured, 5-stage strategic framework to enable African corporate and public entities to embed sustainable ERM architectures aligned with ISO 31000 and COSO standards.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE COMPLIANCE IN STATE-OWNED ENTERPRISES IN UGANDA: A CRITICAL EXAMINATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
summary: This review examines corporate governance compliance in Uganda's state-owned enterprises (SOEs), focusing on board composition and independence, internal audit and controls, transparency and disclosure, accountability, and the relationship between governance arrangements and organizational performance. Uganda's legal framework includes the Public Enterprises Reform and Divestiture Act and the Public Finance Management Act. International standards, particularly the OECD Guidelines on Corporate Governance of State-Owned Enterprises, provide benchmarks on professional state ownership, board autonomy, disclosure, audit and accountability. Uganda-specific literature includes studies of corporate governance and internal audit in SOEs, a case study of the National Water and Sewerage Corporation (NWSC), and research on governance attributes and commercial SOE performance. Official audit material has also reported gaps in consolidation coverage and the absence of a comprehensive database of public corporations and state enterprises. The available evidence suggests that compliance is multidimensional: formal rules are necessary, but their effectiveness depends on professional boards, independent audit, reliable information and follow-through on recommendations. This is a preliminary review, not yet a completed reproducible systematic review: formal multi-database searches, independent screening, quality appraisal and final PRISMA counts must be completed before journal submission. 2. Background State-owned enterprises operate at the intersection of public policy and commercial activity. They may deliver essential services, manage strategic infrastructure, pursue commercial objectives or combine these mandates. Their governance is complex because the state acts as owner on behalf of citizens, while ministries, boards, executives, regulators, auditors and Parliament may exercise different oversight functions. The OECD (2024) observes that this chain of accountability can obscure responsibility and create incentives that do not necessarily serve the long-term interests of the enterprise or the public. Uganda's legal framework recognises both operational autonomy and accountability. The Public Enterprises Reform and Divestiture Act identifies autonomy in operational and financial management, accountability, performance improvement, clear board functions and qualified appointments as important conditions for managing public enterprises. The Public Finance Management Act defines state enterprises to include certain statutory bodies and companies controlled by government and provides a broader framework for public financial management, reporting and internal controls. The existence of rules, however, does not establish that every enterprise implements them effectively.

title: "Digital transformation in accountancy: a study of emerging technologies, adoption challenges, and future implications"
summary: Abstract The field of accountancy has undergone a paradigm shift in the last two decades due to rapid technological advancements. Traditional bookkeeping and manual ledger systems have been replaced by cloud-based accounting software, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics tools. This paper explores the integration of technology in accountancy, examining how automation, AI-driven audit tools, cloud ERP systems, and blockchain are redefining accounting practices. It further analyses the benefits such as enhanced accuracy, real-time reporting, fraud detection, and cost efficiency, alongside challenges including cybersecurity risks, skill gaps, and resistance to change. The study employs a mixed-method approach, reviewing secondary literature and industry reports from 2020-2026 to assess technology adoption trends among small, medium, and large enterprises in India. Findings suggest that while large firms have embraced digital transformation, MSMEs lag due to cost and awareness barriers. The paper concludes that technology in accountancy is no longer optional but a strategic necessity, recommending continuous upskilling, regulatory support, and phased digital adoption for sustainable growth.

title: Controladoria 4.0: como a integração de Big Data e IA redefine o controle financeiro
summary: RESUMO Este estudo analisa como a integração de Big Data e Inteligência Artificial (IA) amplia a atuação da Controladoria 4.0 e modifica a produção e o uso da informação gerencial. A pesquisa adota abordagem qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, com pesquisa bibliográfica e análise documental. A discussão aproxima a Controladoria 4.0 da ideia de Contabilidade 2.0, entendida como a evolução da função contábil pela digitalização, pelo uso de sistemas avançados, de dados em tempo real e de IA. O caso Nike é analisado criticamente a partir de informações atualizadas até setembro de 2026. No exercício de 2026, a empresa registrou receita de US$ 46,4 bilhões; a receita NIKE Direct caiu 6% e as vendas da NIKE Brand Digital recuaram 12%. Em setembro, a Nike foi retirada do índice S&P 100, mas permaneceu listada na New York Stock Exchange. Esses fatos não permitem atribuir causalidade à tecnologia, mas evidenciam que adoção digital e geração de valor não são equivalentes. Conclui-se que a Controladoria 4.0 exige integração entre contabilidade, tecnologia e gestão, com atenção à qualidade dos dados, governança, capacidade analítica e julgamento profissional. Palavras-chave: Controladoria 4.0. Contabilidade 2.0. Big Data. Inteligência Artificial. Transformação digital. ABSTRACT This study analyzes how the integration of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) expands the role of Controllership 4.0 and changes the production and use of managerial information. The research adopts a qualitative, exploratory and descriptive approach, based on bibliographic research and documentary analysis. The discussion connects Controllership 4.0 with the idea of Accounting 2.0, understood as the evolution of the accounting function through digitalization, advanced systems, real-time data and AI. The Nike case is examined critically using information updated through September 2026. In fiscal 2026, the company reported revenue of US$46.4 billion, while NIKE Direct revenue fell 6% and NIKE Brand Digital sales declined 12%. The study highlights that digital adoption and value creation cannot be treated as equivalent. The findings indicate that Controllership 4.0 depends on the integration of accounting, technology and management, together with data quality, governance, analytical capacity and professional judgment. title: Digital Tools for Risk Assessment and Decision-Making in Business Operations
summary: Purpose: This paper analyses how digital tools such as artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and digital twin technologies can enhance risk assessment and decision-making in business operations. Design/Methodology/Approach: The research studies the existing literature on digital transformation and risk management, drawing on 29 publications from 2020 to 2026 (27 journal articles published in the Scopus database and two book chapters). The publications are analysed using thematic synthesis based on three constructs: digital tools, risk assessment capability, and decision-making performance. Research Limitation: The study is based on existing literature, indicating the need for further research on the practical implementation of digital technologies in different business environments. Findings: The results suggest that introducing digital technologies into management systems speeds decision-making, improves risk management, and makes organisations more competitive. Digital technologies enable organisations to process large amounts of real-time data, detect potential risks, and support more informed, timely managerial decisions. Practical Implication: The findings show that digital tools can improve risk assessment procedures and support more effective managerial decision-making. Social Implication: More efficient decision-making and risk management contribute to greater organisational resilience in dynamic business environments. Originality/Value: The study addresses two gaps in the literature: insufficient analysis of technology combinations and the human factor. In its tool-to-capability framework, digital tools contribute to operational performance indirectly by affecting risk assessment and decision-making, an effect the synthesis links to governance and managerial competencies.

title: Orchestrating Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for Adaptive Digital Business Strategy
summary: The rapid acceleration of digital transformation has changed the way organizations formulate and implement business strategies, requiring firms to become more adaptive, data-driven, and responsive to dynamic market conditions. This study aims to examine how big data and artificial intelligence can be orchestrated as integrated strategic capabilities to support adaptive digital business strategy. Using a qualitative conceptual approach, this study applies a structured literature review and thematic synthesis to analyze previous studies related to big data capability, artificial intelligence capability, governance mechanisms, intelligent business insight, and strategic adaptability. The results show that big data functions as a strategic foundation by providing diverse information from customers, markets, operations, and digital platforms, while artificial intelligence acts as an intelligent decision engine that transforms data into predictions, recommendations, automation, and actionable business insights. The findings also indicate that governance and human decision-making are essential in ensuring that the use of big data and AI remains reliable, transparent, accountable, secure, and aligned with organizational objectives. This study concludes that adaptive digital business strategy emerges from the continuous orchestration of data resources, AI systems, governance structures, human judgment, and strategic execution. The proposed framework contributes to digital business literature by explaining how AI-driven big data orchestration can improve decision quality, agility, competitiveness, innovation, operational efficiency, and sustainable digital value creation. In addition, the discussion is expanded to include cybersecurity, data privacy, secure data processing, and AI risk management as critical enablers of large-scale data-driven business systems.

title: Validation of the Model of Financial Reporting Transparency and Accountability in Municipalities from the Perspective of Experts
summary: This study aimed to validate a multidimensional model of financial reporting transparency and accountability in municipalities from the perspective of academic and professional experts. The study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, relevant theoretical sources and previous studies were reviewed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with experts in municipal accounting, auditing, financial management, and public-sector accountability. The interviews continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. The extracted codes were classified into dimensions, components, and indicators, and the reliability of coding was assessed through inter-coder agreement and Cohen’s kappa coefficient. In the quantitative phase, a researcher-made questionnaire based on the qualitative findings was developed and distributed among experts. The fuzzy Delphi technique was used to screen and confirm the indicators, and SmartPLS was applied to assess the measurement and structural validity of the proposed model. The inferential results confirmed the validity of a four-dimensional model including social, economic, organizational, and political dimensions. The inter-coder agreement was 89.6%, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient was 0.804, indicating strong coding reliability. Confirmatory factor analysis showed acceptable factor loadings for the retained indicators. Cronbach’s alpha values ranged from 0.719 to 0.833, composite reliability ranged from 0.735 to 0.846, and AVE values ranged from 0.586 to 0.641, confirming internal consistency and convergent validity. The structural model showed acceptable explanatory power, with R² values of 0.621 for the social dimension, 0.548 for the economic dimension, 0.482 for the organizational dimension, and 0.519 for the political dimension. The Q² values were positive for all dimensions, and the overall GOF index was 0.541, indicating strong model fit. The validated model demonstrates that municipal financial reporting transparency and accountability are multidimensional constructs shaped by social access, economic conditions, organizational capacity, and political-accountability relations. The model can serve as a diagnostic framework for improving reporting quality, public accountability, and financial governance in municipalities

title: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF CASH HOLDINGS IN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND FIRM VALUE: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED SERVICE FIRMS
summary: This study examines the relationship between corporate governance, cash holdings, and firm value among listed service firms in Vietnam. The rapid development of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and financial technology (FinTech), has brought new demands for financial flexibility and corporate governance, particularly in the service sector. This raises an important question of whether firms' cash holding decisions provide a link between corporate governance and firm value. The analysis is based on panel data collected from service firms listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) and the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX) from 2020 to 2024. Corporate governance is measured using five governance characteristics, including board size, board independence, CEO duality, board gender diversity, and foreign ownership. Firm value is proxied by Tobin's Q, while cash holdings are measured as the ratio of cash and cash equivalents to total assets. The empirical procedure involves fixed-effects and random-effects estimations and the Hausman test. FGLS is used after diagnostic tests identify heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation, while the indirect effects are tested using bootstrap analysis. The results are not uniform across the five governance characteristics. CEO duality is positively associated with cash holdings, whereas board gender diversity and foreign ownership are positively associated with firm value. No significant relationship is found between cash holdings and firm value, and the bootstrap results do not support the mediating role of cash holdings. Thus, for the firms in the sample, the evidence points to direct relationships between specific governance characteristics and firm value rather than an indirect relationship through cash holdings. The study adds evidence from Vietnamese listed service firms, a setting that has received relatively limited attention in research on the governance–cash–value relationship. The results also underline the relevance of board composition and ownership structure when firms and policymakers consider measures to improve corporate governance.

title: Designing a blockchain-enabled certification framework for food loss and waste reduction: a proof-of-concept in the fresh food supply chain
summary: Blockchain technology, supported by IoT, has proven essential for improving traceability in food supply chains, but its application to auditing and certifying food loss and waste (FLW) reduction remains largely unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by proposing the architectural design, data models, and audit workflow of a permissioned blockchain-enabled tool developed within the EU H2020 FOODRUS project. Focused on the Spanish fresh vegetable supply chain pilot, the proposed framework integrates Hyperledger Fabric to establish a decentralized and immutable ledger for recording audit evidence and verifying compliance indicators. Rather than assessing long-term operational impact, this study demonstrates the baseline technical feasibility of automating FLW certification workflows through a deployed proof-of-concept prototype. The implementation highlights key architectural contributions, such as standardized data schemas and an integrated 7-stage audit lifecycle, while identifying primary deployment hurdles, notably stakeholder reluctance toward ERP data sharing. The findings confirm that while a permissioned blockchain design effectively secures audit record integrity, broader adoption hinges on establishing legally recognized FLW certification schemes and granular data-governance mechanisms.

title: Employee Capabilities for Digital Service Innovation in Multi-Level Marketing: An Application of Importance - Performance Analysis(IPA)
summary: Digital service innovation has become essential for enhancing customer value and organizational competitiveness. However, research on the capability requirements of multi-level marketing (MLM) practitioners remains limited. Drawing on Service-Dominant Logic, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study identifies four key capability dimensions: Persuasion, Co-creation, Adaptability, and Self-sustainability. Using questionnaire survey data and Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA), the study examines the perceived importance and actual performance of these capabilities to identify management priorities and resource allocation needs. The findings reveal gaps between capability importance and performance, highlighting areas requiring targeted improvement. This study contributes to digital service innovation research in the MLM context and offers practical insights for developing training strategies and capability-building programs to support digital transformation. title: Accounting Compliance And Internal Audit in Public Financial Governance
summary: Penelitian ini mengkaji peran kepatuhan aturan akuntansi dalam memperkuat tata kelola keuangan publik, dengan audit internal berperan sebagai variabel moderator dalam pemerintah daerah. Penelitian ini membahas kesenjangan yang terus berlanjut antara peraturan keuangan formal dan implementasi substansialnya dalam pengelolaan keuangan publik daerah. Dengan menggunakan desain penelitian kuantitatif eksplanatori, penelitian ini dilakukan di Pemerintah Daerah Kabupaten Tapanuli Selatan, Indonesia. Data dikumpulkan dari 93 responden di 31 instansi pemerintah daerah dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kepatuhan akuntansi memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap tata kelola keuangan publik. Audit internal juga menunjukkan pengaruh langsung yang signifikan dan, yang lebih penting, secara signifikan memperkuat hubungan antara kepatuhan akuntansi dan tata kelola keuangan publik. Koefisien determinasi menunjukkan bahwa model yang diusulkan memiliki daya penjelas yang moderat. Temuan ini menemukan bukti bahwa tata kelola keuangan publik yang efektif harus didorong oleh kepatuhan terhadap peraturan, serta adanya penguatan mekanisme pengawasan internal. Studi ini berkontribusi pada literatur akuntansi sektor publik dengan menawarkan model integratif yang menekankan sinergi strategis antara kepatuhan dan audit internal dalam meningkatkan tata kelola keuangan yang berkelanjutan di tingkat pemerintah daerah.

title: Artificial intelligence in corporate legal risk management: A governance and accountability framework
summary: The acceleration of the regulatory requirement, globalization of operations and digital transformation has increased the corporate vulnerability to legal risk. The current legal risk management methods which are mostly reactive and manual fail to handle the scale and complexity of the modern legal and compliance issues. Corporations are in turn moving towards artificial intelligence (AI) more and more as a method of improving legal risk identification, evaluation, and reduction. The paper explores the ways of using AI to balance the control of corporate legal risk and governance, accountability, and ethical responsibility. Using a qualitative and conceptual research of the existing literature, the study examines the major types of corporate legal risk such as regulatory compliance, contractual risk, litigation exposure, governance failures, and data protection issues. The paper examines AI applications within the corporate legal functions, including natural language processing, machine learning, and predictive analytics, and puts into the limelight, how these applications can be used to facilitate proactive and predictive risk management. Meanwhile, the paper critically considers the issues related to the use of AI such as algorithmic bias, transparency, threats to privacy, and legal accountability ambiguity. To resolve the challenges a conceptual framework is suggested, which incorporates the AI capabilities in the corporate level of legal risk management in a regulation-focused and ethically sound framework. The article adds to the literature because it offers a comprehensive view of AI-sensitive law risk management and offers useful data that corporations should consider in terms of finding the balance between innovation and legal accountability.

title: How corporate social irresponsibility erodes consumer trust and shapes consumer responses: a mediation analysis
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to contribute to the emerging corpus of research on corporate social irresponsibility (CSI) and consumer behavior. To this end, this study explores a structural model on the impact of CSI on consumer trust erosion and the subsequent behaviors. It specifically investigates the extent to which CSI impairs consumer trust and addresses the mediating influence of this loss of trust on adverse behaviors, such as boycotting and complaining. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a sample of 204 consumers who have experienced a CSI incident with a brand (in the fashion industry) and uses structural equation modeling to explore relationship pathways and assess significant mediation effects. Findings The results reveal a significant effect between CSI and declining brand trust, increasing consumer complaints. However, this study did not support the expected direct links between CSI and boycotts, as well as between erosion of brand trust and complaints, suggesting that trust erosion facilitates boycott intentions. In contrast, CSI perception fosters complaints. Erosion of brand trust fully mediates the relationship between CSI and boycotts. Research limitations/implications Although this study tackles unexplored areas of consumer behavior, its limitations could offer valuable direction for further research. This study is limited to examining CSI and its impact on trust erosion, complaints and boycotts in the French context. This conceptual framework used can be examined in other contexts to strengthen the findings’ generalizability. Moreover, the model is based on individual responses to CSI by assuming that the dynamics of groups – anti-consumption or resistant communities – have not been included in the comprehensive model (e.g. Dessart et al., 2020; Valor et al., 2022). In addition, it excludes the cultural impact on the mediating construct, namely, trust erosion. Practical implications This study provides actionable guidance for brands to prevent or repair trust erosion following a CSI incident. This guidance comprises prompt public acknowledgment, transparent corrective action and monitoring trust independently of complaint volume, because low complaint levels do not necessarily indicate contained damage. Social implications This study applies psychological contract violation theory to the field of corporate social responsibility (CSR), viewing CSR as an underlying psychological contract between brands, consumers and society, and shows that perceived breaches of this contract as perceived through companies’ wrongdoing can lead to downward spiral in the relationship and result in brand boycott. Originality/value Even though extensive research on brand responsibility is available, the psychological mechanisms underlying consumer responses to CSI remain constrained. This study demonstrates the importance of trust erosion in post-crisis consumer relationships and the need for proactive strategies to attenuate its adverse impacts on consumer behavior.

title: Features of the use of digital tools for engaging young people in physical education and sports
summary: The purpose of the study is to identify the problems and substantiate promising directions for engaging young people in physical education and sports under conditions of digital transformation. Research methods and organization. The work employed methods of theoretical analysis of scientific literature, content analysis of regulatory legal acts, systemic and comparative analysis of digital sports services, and generalization and synthesis of empirical data. The empirical base was made up of regulatory legal documents of the Russian Federation, official statistical data of the Ministry of Sports of the Russian Federation, Rosstat, and the Unified Interdepartmental Information and Statistical System for the period 2020–2024, the results of sociological studies by VCIOM and FOM, as well as scientific publications by domestic and foreign authors for 2020–2025. Data processing was carried out using methods of systemic and logical analysis. Research results and conclusions. The main barriers of the digital environment hindering the physical activity of young people were identified (competition from digital leisure, the formation of sedentary behavior, and the unreliability of information); promising directions for the use of digital tools were substantiated: the creation of a unified federal digital platform, the development of phygital formats and hybrid classes, and the popularization of physical activity through digital media. The strategic task of the current period lies in the synergetic integration of the digital environment and physical activity, in which digital technologies become a tool for increasing motivation and accessibility of classes for the younger generation.
